before.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

before.supportingExcerpt: The branch experiments further narrowed an invasive-morphology question in MDA-MB-231. Blocking the geranylgeranylation branch had a larger effect than the tested sterol-branch block, and GGPP partly restored invasive growth after mutant-p53 depletion or statin treatment. That is not evidence that GGPP rescues inhibition of the transferase itself, nor that every effect in both cell lines was entirely explained by one metabolite. The authors allowed contributions from other products. In a fictional supply comparison, synthesis falls under an inhibitor in both lipid-poor and lipid-rich medium, but growth slows mainly in the former while import is stipulated to compensate in the latter. Equal engagement with different growth outcomes is compatible with environmental supply; it is not a measurement of supply or dependence in a person's tumour.

before.supportingExcerpt: In the fictional supply experiment, nuclear SREBP-2 and uptake messages respond to lipid-poor medium; external lipid supply can reduce the response and compensate for synthesis perturbation. Assess precursor and nuclear regulator, responsive transcripts, cellular sterols and uptake separately from labelled synthesis rates. Use controlled supplementation to test the proposed bottleneck; total amount does not specify production or local sensing. Lower synthesis does not itself show that a compound bound its target, and a medium effect does not identify uptake as its cause. An uncharacterised SCAP or MTOR variant needs evidence for its proposed functional effect; a gene name alone assigns neither activation nor loss of function.

before.supportingExcerpt: The branch experiments further narrowed an invasive-morphology question in MDA-MB-231. Blocking the geranylgeranylation branch had a larger effect than the tested sterol-branch block, and GGPP partly restored invasive growth after mutant-p53 depletion or statin treatment. before.supportingExcerpt: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase upstream in the mevalonate pathway, which supplies cholesterol and nonsterol products. In Freed-Pastor and colleagues' breast-cancer 3D cultures, geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate partially rescued an invasive phenotype after mutant-p53 depletion or simvastatin treatment. This illustrates why mevalonate rescue alone cannot uniquely attribute an effect to cholesterol. It does not identify every relevant metabolite, establish a universal cancer dependency or show that a statin perturbation reproduces every change in SCAP-SREBP regulation.
before.explanation: Mevalonate restores several branches. Controlled branch perturbations, selective add-backs and direct metabolite measurements can narrow causality; the rescue alone does not identify cholesterol or clinical exposure. before.supportingExcerpt: HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate and is inhibited by statins. The downstream pathway branches: farnesyl pyrophosphate, FPP, feeds sterol synthesis through squalene and GGPP production as well as supplying protein prenylation; geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, GGPP, supplies another prenylation route. before.supportingExcerpt: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.
before.explanation: Energy rate, captured transcripts, chemical species and compartment, stress protection and lipid-driven death need separate measurements. before.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. before.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

before.supportingExcerpt: Yap 2023 reported phase 1 IACS-010759 studies in 17 people with acute myeloid leukaemia and 23 with advanced solid tumours. Elevated blood lactate and neurotoxicity limited exposure needed for sustained complex-I inhibition; target inhibition was modest, antitumour activity limited, no recommended phase 2 dose was established and both studies were discontinued. These named safety and exposure results separate a model vulnerability from a usable treatment. A respiratory RNA signature plus a lower ATP-based signal still establishes neither increased oxygen-consumption rate nor counted cell death. Measure identified viable cells, normalised oxygen use, engagement and independent growth or death outcomes. Acidification can include respiratory carbon dioxide as well as glycolysis, and lactate production with oxygen can coexist with respiration.
before.explanation: Stable viable counts with lower ATP-associated signal do not establish cell killing. Regrowth concerns survivors, while probe chemistry and compartment validation are needed before assigning a reactive species or mitochondrial origin. Source keys: 32130885. Claim type: premise-backed-fictional-reasoning. Exact field containment is checked separately from this semantic disposition; source and inference depths are retained.

before.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

before.supportingExcerpt: The branch experiments further narrowed an invasive-morphology question in MDA-MB-231. before.supportingExcerpt: HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate and is inhibited by statins. The downstream pathway branches: farnesyl pyrophosphate, FPP, feeds sterol synthesis through squalene and GGPP production as well as supplying protein prenylation; geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, GGPP, supplies another prenylation route. Farnesyl and geranylgeranyl lipid modifications help position specified RAS- and RHO-family proteins, respectively. Cholesterol is a membrane component and a precursor of steroid hormones. before.supportingExcerpt: Freed-Pastor 2012 studied mutant-p53 breast cancer cells in three-dimensional culture, with different outcomes in two triple-negative lines. Depleting mutant p53 reduced invasive behaviour in MDA-MB-231 but did not make it form ordered hollow acini; MDA-MB-468 could acquire a more ordered, hollow architecture. Statins reduced invasion in the former and caused growth inhibition with extensive death in the latter, rather than exactly reproducing every p53-depletion phenotype. Mutant-p53 depletion reduced mevalonate-pathway expression, and mevalonate add-back opposed several statin effects. This supports a pathway contribution in the studied systems without isolating cholesterol. The whole paper also examined growth, death and xenograft growth; it was not solely an architecture experiment, and none of these results established patient treatment benefit.

before.supportingExcerpt: Freed-Pastor 2012 studied mutant-p53 breast cancer cells in three-dimensional culture, with different outcomes in two triple-negative lines. Depleting mutant p53 reduced invasive behaviour in MDA-MB-231 but did not make it form ordered hollow acini; MDA-MB-468 could acquire a more ordered, hollow architecture. Statins reduced invasion in the former and caused growth inhibition with extensive death in the latter, rather than exactly reproducing every p53-depletion phenotype. Mutant-p53 depletion reduced mevalonate-pathway expression, and mevalonate add-back opposed several statin effects. This supports a pathway contribution in the studied systems without isolating cholesterol. The whole paper also examined growth, death and xenograft growth; it was not solely an architecture experiment, and none of these results established patient treatment benefit.

before.supportingExcerpt: Echeverria 2019 treated three patient-derived triple-negative breast cancer xenograft models with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Barcode structure was broadly maintained at the residual nadir; regrowth could select dominant barcodes, so this does not exclude all clonal selection. In PIM001-P, the RNA analysis highlighted oxidative phosphorylation and isolated residual cells had higher oxygen consumption and lower extracellular acidification than untreated cells. Those rate measurements were not obtained in every model. IACS-010759 delayed regrowth after chemotherapy in the three tested models, rather than eradicating the tumours. Regrown models could again respond to chemotherapy. Two serial human biopsy cases supported stability during initial AC but did not establish invariant clones through all subsequent treatment. Rate, state, perturbation response and clinical benefit remain distinct evidence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

points.requirement: An altered base, a bulky adduct, a copying mismatch and a double-strand break are physically different lesions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A DNA lesion is a physical or chemical problem; a mutation is a lasting sequence change. Repair can remove damage before a mutation is fixed. Recognition and checkpoint signaling are responses to the problem, whereas successful repair, tolerated damage, arrest and death are separate outcomes. The lesson map therefore ends by measuring the outcome instead of assuming that the alarm completed the repair.

Selected repair jobs address different problems: base excision begins by removing a damaged base, nucleotide excision removes a lesion-containing stretch, and mismatch repair corrects copying mismatches. Lindahl purified an E. coli enzyme that released uracil without cutting the DNA backbone, a specific early base-excision step rather than proof of all human repair routes. Double-strand breaks can use matching-template homologous repair or end joining. These are selected jobs, not exclusive assignments of every lesion to one pathway.

Gamma-H2AX is histone H2AX phosphorylated at serine 139. Rogakou 1998 observed a rapid response after experimentally induced double-strand breaks in mammalian systems. A microscopy focus is a response around damage, not direct sequencing of a break or a universal repair-failure test. In a fictional culture with a bulky lesion and increased gamma-H2AX, measure lesion removal over time with suitable controls before claiming nucleotide-excision failure, homologous repair deficiency or drug sensitivity.

Platinum agents can form DNA crosslinks; interstrand links block strand separation and require coordinated repair machinery. The Fanconi pathway links DNA-processing activities, and homologous repair can contribute to resolving replication-associated damage. This does not mean every platinum lesion is an interstrand link or that every HR-deficient tumor responds. A repair mechanism, an observed drug effect and clinical benefit in a defined population need separate evidence.
evidence.explanation: The selected jobs retain damaged base, lesion-containing stretch, copying mismatch and double-strand break as distinct inputs. points.requirement: The selected sister-template repair route is conditional on a suitable template after DNA copying, not every break or cell state.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.
evidence.explanation: A matching template and cell-cycle/substrate conditions qualify the selected sister-chromatid route. evidence.supportingExcerpt:

A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. BRCA1 and BRCA2 name genes everyone normally carries. Interpret a reported variant by its classification, sample and origin, then assess the remaining allele and repair function. An uncertain BRCA2 variant with no normal sample and no remaining-copy assessment establishes neither inheritance nor biallelic loss nor current repair deficiency. BRCA1 and BRCA2 have different repair roles. Brca1-deficient mouse embryonic stem cells had impaired homologous repair of defined chromosome breaks in Moynahan 1999. These model-specific results do not determine the effect of every human variant; the matching-template diagram omits many preparation and finishing steps.

In the CIMBA analysis, the invasive-breast-cancer results included 3,797 BRCA1 and 2,392 BRCA2 carriers, with individual marker data available for varying subsets. Among tumors with relevant marker information, 68% in BRCA1 carriers and 16% in BRCA2 carriers were triple-negative. These are pathology proportions among cancers in mutation carriers, not the chance that an individual carrier develops cancer or that a person with triple-negative disease carries a BRCA variant. Age and ascertainment matter.

Repair capacity can change after treatment. In the selected eight-person resistant metastatic breast cancer cohort of Waks 2020, four acquired definite or putative BRCA reversions; other mechanisms could restore repair too. A reversion can restore a disrupted reading frame, while old genomic patterns remain. This selected cohort does not establish a common or most-frequent mechanism across all breast cancers, and a single tissue or blood sample can miss heterogeneous reversions.

points.requirement: BRCA1 and BRCA2 have distinct supported repair roles; a single finding or VUS does not establish biallelic HR deficiency.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
BRCA1 and BRCA2 name genes everyone normally carries. Interpret a reported variant by its classification, sample and origin, then assess the remaining allele and repair function. An uncertain BRCA2 variant with no normal sample and no remaining-copy assessment establishes neither inheritance nor biallelic loss nor current repair deficiency. Tumor purity and complex copy-number states can limit allele interpretation.

BRCA1 and BRCA2 have different repair roles. Brca1-deficient mouse embryonic stem cells had impaired homologous repair of defined chromosome breaks in Moynahan 1999. Purified full-length human BRCA2 promoted RAD51 assembly on single-stranded DNA in Jensen 2010. These model-specific results do not determine the effect of every human variant; the matching-template diagram omits many preparation and finishing steps.

In the CIMBA analysis, the invasive-breast-cancer results included 3,797 BRCA1 and 2,392 BRCA2 carriers, with individual marker data available for varying subsets. Among tumors with relevant marker information, 68% in BRCA1 carriers and 16% in BRCA2 carriers were triple-negative. These are pathology proportions among cancers in mutation carriers, not the chance that an individual carrier develops cancer or that a person with triple-negative disease carries a BRCA variant. Age and ascertainment matter.

Repair capacity can change after treatment. In the selected eight-person resistant metastatic breast cancer cohort of Waks 2020, four acquired definite or putative BRCA reversions; other mechanisms could restore repair too. A reversion can restore a disrupted reading frame, while old genomic patterns remain. This selected cohort does not establish a common or most-frequent mechanism across all breast cancers, and a single tissue or blood sample can miss heterogeneous reversions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

points.requirement: Compatible ligatable blunt ends can be joined without sequence loss; c-NHEJ is not always inaccurate.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.
evidence.explanation: Compatible-end preservation is explicit alongside processed joining, so classical joining is not defined as obligatorily inaccurate. evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. points.requirement: Under stated IdU-then-CldU 30-minute pulses and 2 kb per micrometre calibration, fictional 15 and 7.5 micrometre second tracks yield 1 and 0.5 kb/min.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Replication stress concerns difficulty copying DNA, including slow or stalled forks. A stalled fork can be protected and restart; it is not automatically a broken chromosome. Checkpoint activation, recovery, incomplete copying, damage and death are separate stages and measurements. High checkpoint-gene RNA or rapid proliferation alone does not establish fork stress, dependence or drug sensitivity.

RPA coats exposed single-stranded DNA and helps recruit ATR through ATRIP, initiating checkpoint signaling in biochemical and cellular experiments. Activated H-Ras in normal human-cell models produced hyper-replication before damage signaling and senescence. Bester studied HPV E6/E7 or cyclin-E-driven models in which nucleotide limitation disturbed replication and nucleoside supplementation in culture improved dynamics. These experiments do not recommend supplements or predict the behavior of every oncogene-bearing tumor.

In a fictional DNA-combing exercise, live cells receive a 30-minute IdU pulse followed by a 30-minute CldU pulse. At the stated example stretching calibration of 2 kilobases per micrometre, a 7.5-micrometre second track represents 15 kilobases copied in 30 minutes, or 0.5 kilobases per minute; a 15-micrometre track gives 1 kilobase per minute. Bester used those pulse times and calibration, but these example lengths are not that study's results and the calibration is not universal.

DNA-fiber measurements require viable cells that incorporate labels; extraction destroys sampled cells. Ordinary fixed pathology cannot retrospectively supply live-label tracks. Document pulse timing, labeling, stretching, track selection, cell-cycle distribution, model and comparison group. A lower population S-phase fraction is distinct from the speed of one selected molecule. Track length alone establishes neither the cause, breaks, restart nor death; checkpoint dependence needs a targeted perturbation and a separate functional outcome, without a universal patient-positive cutoff.

points.requirement: Electron transfer toward oxygen and water is distinct from proton pumping from matrix to intermembrane space; not every respiratory complex pumps.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In mitochondria, respiratory electron transfer and proton movement are distinct processes. Some respiratory complexes move protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space; return through ATP synthase can support ATP formation, while other return pathways dissipate the gradient without that synthesis step. These directions do not specify a fixed proton-to-ATP ratio. Protons return from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the membrane-embedded Fo part of ATP synthase. The matrix-facing F1 part uses the transferred energy to make ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. Protons provide the driving force; they are not converted into ATP. A parallel proton leak bypasses ATP synthase and dissipates the gradient. In Racker and Stoeckenius' reconstituted vesicles, a light-driven membrane system from Halobacterium supported ATP formation when mitochondrial ATPase was included. Their artificial vesicles pumped in the opposite direction to the intact source cells, so the experiment supports coupling without specifying a universal cellular orientation or ratio.

points.requirement: Qualitative local sterol supply and a separate Insig-associated ER-retention condition are not a whole-cell gauge, numerical threshold or absolute transport rule.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Lipid metabolism includes synthesis, uptake, storage, membrane remodelling and oxidation. Cholesterol regulation and fatty-acid regulation overlap but are not interchangeable. Identify the SREBP member, cellular compartment and measured output rather than treating a transcript, precursor, nuclear fragment, sterol amount and synthesis rate as the same observation. SCAP-SREBP transport responds to endoplasmic reticulum cholesterol in the cited cell experiments. The mevalonate pathway supplies sterols and nonsterol products, including substrates for protein prenylation. Rescue by mevalonate therefore cannot uniquely identify cholesterol as the limiting product. Transcript abundance, lipid abundance, labelled production and a controlled survival-dependence experiment answer different questions. Results from a particular cell model or mouse experiment do not establish a universal tumour vulnerability or a preferred diet or treatment.

points.requirement: An acetyl mark, its BET reader and a mark-writing process are distinct.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
BRD4 is a chromatin reader that recognizes acetylated histones and helps regulate transcription. Its recognition pockets and other protein interactions can contribute different functions.

Engaging an acetyl-recognition pocket and depleting a whole protein are different interventions. In selected TNBC models with acquired BET-inhibitor resistance, cells remained dependent on BRD4 through bromodomain-independent regulation. Verify pocket engagement and depletion independently before comparing growth outcomes. Neither operation alone establishes clinical benefit or a vulnerability caused by an uncharacterized BET-family variant.

BET proteins read acetylated lysine marks; they do not write the acetyl mark. The family includes BRD2, BRD3, BRD4 and BRDT, with two bromodomains and an extra-terminal interaction region. BRD4 can recruit transcription-elongation machinery, but other bromodomain proteins are not all BET proteins and family members are not functionally interchangeable. A schematic that retains the same histone mark during pocket occupation and protein depletion isolates two different interventions. The fixed mark is a drawing convention rather than a measured unchanged acetylation state; the state of the mark needs its own measurement. A representative pocket also does not make JQ1 specific to BD1.

In a fictional culture, an engaged BET pocket probe leaves growth unchanged while independently controlled BRD4 depletion impairs growth. The findings can coexist if the remaining protein supplies functions the probe does not block, as the resistant-model work illustrates. Binding assays, chromatin occupancy, early RNA changes, later growth and death, general transcription effects and appropriate restoration controls answer different questions. Lower MYC RNA alone does not attribute a later effect to MYC.

French identified a BRD4-NUT fusion in the defined carcinoma; a fusion is a different biological alteration from an ordinary sequence variant. Stathis reported four people with confirmed BRD4-NUT carcinomas treated with OTX015/MK-8628 in compassionate use: two had rapid regression, with no randomized comparison or established survival benefit. The report described thrombocytopenia, including reversible grade 3 events and a grade 4 event in one patient. This small selected series does not establish efficacy across BET-altered tumors.

points.requirement: The common ligand-dependent Notch route uses membrane-bound ligand on a sender contacting a receptor on a separate receiver membrane, not membrane fusion or a free secreted ligand.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A ligand-bearing sender, receptor amount, received signal and growth dependence are separate observations. Locate malignant, vessel and other neighboring cells before assigning a Notch mechanism. Ligand on a vessel is not evidence that the tumor received the signal, and total receptor is different from a released nuclear intracellular domain.

Common contact-dependent Notch signaling begins when Delta-like or Jagged ligand on one cell engages a receptor on a neighbor. Ligand-regulated extracellular cleavage permits subsequent gamma-secretase-mediated membrane cleavage; the released Notch intracellular domain, NICD, can enter the nucleus and work with transcriptional partners. This route differs from an RTK phosphorylation relay and omits receptor maturation and sender mechanics.

Weng found activating NOTCH1 changes in extracellular heterodimerization or PEST regions in more than half of the studied T-ALLs. Agrawal identified predicted inactivating alterations in head-and-neck squamous tumors, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role there. An uncharacterized allele inherits neither direction from the pathway name; tissue, cell identity and alteration effect matter.

A fictional T-ALL culture with high nuclear NICD without a ligand-bearing neighbor, and lower NICD after gamma-secretase blockade, supports a ligand-independent activation hypothesis. A contact-blocking experiment that lowers NICD without changing growth instead supports reduced received signaling without demonstrating a growth requirement. Control general toxicity, contact conditions, independent pathway perturbations and compensation. Gamma-secretase also processes other proteins; responsive HES/HEY RNA and nuclear staining need validated assays and are not universal eligibility cutoffs.

points.requirement: Under the same stipulated upstream secretion block, intact destruction control and a downstream escape can yield different canonical beta-catenin nuclear outputs.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.

points.requirement: Vessel structures, actual flow, tracer delivery and oxygenation are separate observations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Angiogenesis creates new vessels from existing vessels through endothelial-cell growth and signalling, including VEGF and its receptors. It also occurs in development and repair. A tumour can obtain blood by other routes: Holash and colleagues observed co-option of existing vessels in their tumour models. Vessel structure, perfusion, permeability, tracer transport and oxygenation are separate measurements. Density counts structures within an area; perfusion concerns blood flow through a region; permeability concerns material crossing vessel walls; a tracer readout follows a particular probe. Oxygen availability also depends on diffusion and cellular consumption.

points.requirement: Blood delivery, tissue diffusion distance and local cellular demand can create uneven oxygen availability.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Hypoxia is reduced local oxygen availability relative to tissue needs. It is different from complete absence of oxygen and from a permanent defect in mitochondria. Delivery, functioning vessels, diffusion distance and oxygen consumption all matter, and conditions change across regions and time. Removing tissue interrupts delivery, so collection and handling can change the state being studied.

points.requirement: Conceptual oxygen marks and HIF or RNA responses are not calibrated oxygen readings, universal distance thresholds or oxygen-exposure treatment recommendations.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: HIF-1 contains alpha and beta protein subunits. Under oxygen-replete conditions, oxygen-dependent modification of the alpha subunit enables VHL-associated degradation; limiting that regulation can stabilise it. Jaakkola and the Semenza review describe this mechanism and additional regulation. HIF RNA, alpha-protein stability and the resulting transcriptional response are different quantities. Alternative molecular regulation can alter HIF, so neither protein staining nor an RNA signature is a calibrated oxygen meter.
evidence.explanation: HIF/RNA outputs and oxygen symbols are not calibrated oxygen, a universal distance or an exposure recommendation. points.requirement: The specified Hanahan 2022 framework separates population capabilities, enabling processes and tissue participants rather than twelve equivalent hallmarks.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The hallmarks are a versioned research framework, not a diagnostic checklist, stage, clinical assay standard or a demand that every cell independently perform every capability. The 2000 proposal contained six capabilities. The 2011 account retained six, added two emerging capabilities and described two enabling characteristics. In the 2022 account, the two emerging capabilities joined the eight core capabilities.

Normal renewal also involves division, so speed alone, one broken rule or one molecular result does not define cancer. Benign growths can cause harm through their size or location. Blood cancers such as leukaemia need not form a solid lump and can disrupt normal blood production.
